title: The Gray Portrait
hook: The old museum guard left me one rule: if the woman in the gray portrait ever looks at you, don't look away first.
lines: I guard a small art museum at night. Forty paintings, one long hallway... and me.
The old guard left me one rule, scratched into the back of my badge.
The woman in the gray portrait always looks at the window. If she ever looks at you... don't look away first.
For two months, she just stared at that window. Pale face. Gray dress. Hands folded in her lap.
Then, one rainy night, I swept my flashlight across her frame...
And her eyes were on me.
I froze. I stared back. My eyes burned, and watered... and I didn't dare blink.
Then my radio crackled, right on my belt.
I looked down. Just for a second.
When I looked up... the frame was empty.
Then everything went cold. And still. And I couldn't lift my hands from my lap.
They hired a new guard this week. Young. Nervous. He reads the back of his badge every night.
Tonight, he walked past with his flashlight... and I turned my eyes from the window... to him.
